data.body:
ADR SOURCE MATERIAL FOR S9 — PART 3/4: OPERATIONAL FINDINGS · DOC CORRECTIONS · THE TIER MODEL

## 3.1 The IMDS hop-limit constraint — AND THE CRUCIAL CORRECTION
WARNING: THIS TICKET'S FRAMING IS WRONG ON ONE POINT. The contingency NEVER FIRED. No metadata_options
terraform change was made, and no ADR 0046 entry was written.
The constraint as stated (9249): "main.tf:50-54 sets http_tokens = 'required' and leaves
http_put_response_hop_limit unset (default 1, which normally blocks the extra Docker-bridge hop), and
pyproject.toml's reviewbot comment says the journald fallback exists because 'in-container IMDS is
unreachable' — yet docker-compose.yml:157-158 documents the opcert container fetching SSM keys with boto3
where 'the instance profile supplies the credentials via IMDS', which only works if IMDS IS reachable."
=> THE MANIFESTATION WAS A DOCUMENTARY CONTRADICTION IN THE TREE, NOT A CREDENTIAL FAILURE.
Default position taken BEFORE measuring: "The opcert container's working instance-profile SSM fetch is
direct evidence, and it is stronger evidence than the pyproject.toml remark."
The contingency was pre-decided IN FULL so nothing was deferred to the executor, with a bounded-exposure
argument: "docker-compose.yml defines no networks: section, so gerrit, review-bot, and opcert already
share one default bridge, and all three are first-party rebar components that already receive
instance-role-derived secrets through the .env that fetch-secrets.sh writes. Raising the hop limit
therefore widens reach to containers that are already inside the same trust boundary."
THE MEASUREMENT (operator-attested, SSM on i-00880b2c7f13527c5, 896586841071/us-east-1):
    === AC1 — IMDSv2 token request from INSIDE the review-bot container ===
      http_status=200   token_len=56   role=rebar-gerrit-instance-role
"DECISION RECORDED: this selects the IAM-only path; the hop-limit contingency did NOT fire, so the
conditional HttpPutResponseHopLimit == 2 criterion is vacuous."
THE CONTAINMENT IS "MEASURE FIRST, CHANGE NOTHING." Honest ADR content: IMDS IS reachable from containers
at hop limit 1 (measured); the exception was pre-authorized with a bounded-exposure rationale and was NOT
needed; the standing exposure fact is the flat single-bridge compose topology.
AND THE pyproject.toml COMMENT WAS WRONG ABOUT ITS OWN CAUSE (a574): "the review bot's CloudWatch voter
metrics (voter.py:95/110/151/215) silently no-op for the SAME missing-region reason. Their comments blame
IMDS reachability, which the above shows is not the cause." Cite as an example of an unevidenced in-tree
comment misdirecting a design.

## 3.2 Bedrock region resolution — VERIFIED, with a subtler reason than expected
(a) IMDS supplies NO region. 9249: "inside that container boto3.session.Session().region_name is None and
    boto3.client('bedrock-runtime') raises NoRegionError... So region discovery does NOT come from
    instance metadata here: raising the hop limit would fix credential reachability and still leave the
    region unresolved. The two concerns are INDEPENDENT... Every Bedrock probe in this epic passed an
    explicit region_name argument, which is why this stayed invisible until it was measured directly."
    Mechanism (a574): "botocore's IMDSRegionProvider is wired ONLY into the smart-defaults path
    (defaults_mode=auto), so a reachable IMDS supplies credentials but never a region."
(b) rebar's own knob alone was NOT sufficient. a574 verbatim: "setting ONLY REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION was
    NOT sufficient. I set it, restarted the service, and boto3 STILL raised NoRegionError — because that
    is rebar's OWN knob and boto3 has never heard of it. rebar's path worked (it threads the value into
    BedrockProvider) while every other AWS caller in the image stayed region-less. AC4's insistence on a
    BARE boto3 client with no explicit region is exactly what exposed the conflation. Both vars are now
    set and they are NOT interchangeable."
(c) AWS_REGION ALONE DOES NOT WORK on this botocore. MEASURED: "AWS_REGION=us-east-1 only ->
    Session().region_name is None -> NoRegionError; AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=eu-west-1 -> region_name ==
    'eu-west-1'. botocore's session-variable table (configprovider.py:74) maps region to
    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION only." VERSION-SCOPED: boto3/botocore 1.43.58 — carry that qualifier.
    Two rebar docstrings were factually wrong and were corrected: bedrock_model.py:50-51, config.py:19-20.
(d) THE EXCEPTION THAT ESCAPES IS NOT NoRegionError: "pydantic-ai already catches botocore's NoRegionError
    at providers/bedrock.py:463 and re-raises pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError... The REAL defect is
    narrower: UserError is NOT a subclass of rebar's LLMError/LLMUnavailableError, so no except LLMError
    handler in rebar catches it — including the review bot's fail-closed path."
(e) The preflight oracle is boto3.session.Session().region_name, NOT env sniffing: "a read-only property...
    measured at 0.002s. Hand-rolling os.environ.get('AWS_REGION') would report a region that boto3 then
    refuses." bedrock_model.py:78.
(f) SEVERITY: "That is a HARD failure at client construction, before any model call, and story eb6e ships
    the cutover with NO cross-provider fallback. So flipping REBAR_LLM_MODEL to bedrock:... without also
    setting a region takes the LLM-Review gate down for every landing rather than degrading it."
(g) DURABILITY: "/opt/rebar is a DEPLOYED COPY, not a git checkout, so the in-place edit alone would have
    been reverted by the next deploy."
(h) THE STRONGEST METHODOLOGICAL LESSON IN THE EPIC: "the runbook ENCODED THE BLIND SPOT: every probe in it
    passes --region explicitly, so none ever exercised ambient resolution. That is precisely why
    NoRegionError survived an entire epic of Bedrock verification."

## 3.3 Caching and inference profiles — the measured relationship
NOT mutually exclusive; only inference profiles are invokable at all. eb6e: "ON-DEMAND MODEL IDS ARE NOT
INVOKABLE AT ALL, so the on-demand-vs-profile comparison the hedge contemplates is moot." And "PROMPT
CACHING WORKS WITH A REGIONAL INFERENCE PROFILE: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 measured cache_write=4017
on attempt 1 and cached on attempt 2. They are NOT mutually exclusive."
THIS REFUTES THE ISSUE THE EPIC WAS BUILT AROUND (2932): "This refutes the premise of pydantic-ai #4381 for
this model/region — the issue this story was built around does not reproduce."
CACHING IS MODEL-DEPENDENT AND FAILS SILENTLY; the discriminator is the MODEL, not the profile prefix.
2932: "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0 AND global.anthropic... both returned cache_read=0 AND
cache_write=0 on both attempts, with the full 4029 input tokens billed every call — no error, no warning.
CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST INFERENCE: I initially attributed this to the global. prefix; a controlled
same-model comparison showed BOTH fail, so the discriminator is the MODEL, not the profile prefix. This
silent double-billing is the real hazard #4381 is circling."
Hence Decision B (the cache-zero warning) and why it cannot reuse _warn_if_zeroed_usage: "That guard fires
on requests > 0 AND input_tokens == 0 AND output_tokens == 0. The measured Bedrock failure is the OPPOSITE
shape: input_tokens=4029 with cache_read=0 and cache_write=0. The existing predicate never fires."
Also: "us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0 with a cachePoint hard-fails: AccessDeniedException: You
invoked an unsupported model or your request did not allow prompt caching."
END TO END THROUGH REBAR (7a79, 19-call gate run): cache_read_tokens=542,723 cache_write_tokens=6,239. Raw
boto3, 29,400-char repeated prefix: sonnet-4-6 cacheWrite=6604 then cacheRead=6604; opus-4-8
cacheWrite=11404 then cacheRead=11404. "pydantic-ai's Bedrock adapter does map
cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens (models/bedrock.py:676-682), so these are real numbers."
THE cachePoint TTL PREMISE WAS WRONG AND IS NOW CORRECTED (1aa2): "Bedrock's cachePoint block takes an
OPTIONAL ttl that DEFAULTS TO 5 MINUTES — the same default Anthropic's cache_control applies. The TTL is
not missing on Bedrock; it is defaulted, and defaulted to the SAME value... There is no observable
difference to account for, and no per-provider cache tuning is needed. Bedrock additionally offers a
1-hour TTL for some Claude models. It is opt-in and rebar does not request it, so it is not a difference
either. Sources: AWS 'Amazon Bedrock now supports 1-hour duration for prompt caching' (Jan 2026) and the
Bedrock cachePoint API reference." Honest limit: "no gate run exercises a gap LONGER than 5 minutes... the
runs confirm the lifetime is not shorter than a gate run; they do not probe expiry."
=> SUPERSEDES the "Bedrock cachePoint carries no TTL" claim which appears in 0d76 comments 18/19/20, on
   061c's own final comment, and in 1aa2's description. DO NOT CARRY THE OLD VERSION INTO THE ADR.
rebar never writes the raw wire key: grep cachePoint across src/ returns nothing.

## 3.4 Bedrock model-id constraints (the trap set)
- Plain foundation-model ids are refused on-demand: "Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput
  isn't supported. Retry your request with the ID or ARN of an inference profile." "Any Bedrock example
  config that omits the us. prefix is broken on arrival."
- list-foundation-models IS A TRAP: "it enumerates on-demand FOUNDATION models, not INFERENCE PROFILES,
  and the us.-prefixed profile id is exactly the form that is not a foundation model."
- global. inference profiles are a valid MEASURED form in 896586841071 — do not pin us. in IAM.
- VERSIONED Bedrock ids break provider qualification (3768): "_resolve_target's 'already
  provider-qualified' test is ':' in model, and a versioned Bedrock id contains a colon in its version
  suffix, so the configured provider='bedrock' was silently dropped." -> bug 03b0. Operational sting: "the
  canonical id is what the AWS console and docs display, so ...-v1:0 is the string an operator will paste."
- THE INVERSE ALSO BITES (8455): unversioned haiku is INVALID on Bedrock; the valid form carries the
  version suffix -> ValidationException: The provided model identifier is invalid.
- temperature is FATAL on some Bedrock models: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 + temperature=0 -> 400
  "'temperature' is deprecated for this model"; identical call without it succeeds. Root asymmetry:
  "_drop_unsupported_sampling_settings exists ONLY in pydantic-ai's models/anthropic.py, NOT in
  models/bedrock.py — so the direct-Anthropic path degrades gracefully and the Bedrock path hard-fails."

## 3.5 IAM, account, identity
- Account/region for ALL landed work: 896586841071 / us-east-1.
- THE WRONG-ACCOUNT INCIDENT (2932/0d76), verbatim: "IMPORTANT CORRECTION — my Bedrock measurements were
  taken in a DIFFERENT AWS ACCOUNT AND REGION than this project's infrastructure. I did not check this
  before recording them as findings, and the operator caught it." Wrong place: account 5797...98, region
  us-east-2, IAM user joe_sec with AmazonBedrockFullAccess. "Bedrock model access is enabled per account
  AND per region." Re-measurement was assigned to 0d76/9249 and completed.
- Policy: rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse, inline on rebar-gerrit-instance-role, in a NEW iam_s7.tf (the
  single-owner contract at iam.tf:4-9 forbids editing iam.tf). Actions InvokeModel +
  InvokeModelWithResponseStream. bedrock:Converse deliberately NOT granted: "it is not the action checked,
  and granting an unused action is blast radius for nothing."
- BOTH resource wildcards are load-bearing: region wildcard "because a cross-region inference profile
  invokes the foundation model in its member regions"; the *. profile-prefix wildcard "because global.
  inference profiles are a valid MEASURED form." "The region field is wildcarded; the MODEL is not."
- Pre-change baseline recorded so the delta is unambiguous: all four actions implicitDeny. "The grant was
  genuinely additive."
- NEGATIVE CONTROL (the least-privilege oracle): "converse to amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 returns
  AccessDeniedException naming bedrock:InvokeModel on the nova ARN — so the Claude-only scope genuinely
  binds."
- Tooling gotchas now in the runbook: aws-cli 2.33.15 on this AMI exposes NO bedrock-runtime streaming
  subcommand ("An unknown subcommand exits printing the CLI help stub, which reads like a failed call");
  SSM AWS-RunShellScript mangles embedded JSON through shell quoting — base64-encode the script; THE
  REVIEW-BOT IMAGE SHIPS NO aws CLI, which made one AC "unsatisfiable by construction."
  --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out is needed for invoke-model's --body, NOT for converse;
  "--inference-config may be passed ONCE only — giving it twice is rejected client-side with Unknown
  options, which looks like an API refusal and is not one."

## 3.6 The Pass-1 archaeology (77ed) — the most consequential silent regression
3,843 plan-review REVIEW_RESULT sidecars by recorded data.model, by day:
  2026-06-24..27: opus 16, 32, 25, 42 | sonnet 0
  2026-06-28:     opus 37            | sonnet 20 (transition)
  2026-06-29 on:  opus 0             | sonnet 87, 78, ... (2,710 sonnet runs since)
"115 opus runs before the change, ZERO after. A total, permanent changeover one day after the commit."
Cause: 4beec08a4 (2026-06-27) introduced _verifier_cfg passed as the WHOLE RUN's cfg, and
PydanticAIRunner.run then discarded req.config. "git log -L62,66 on plan-review.yaml shows Pass-1 has
declared the cheapest rung since the workflow was born and has NEVER ONCE actually run on it."
WHY THE LADDER DOES NOT SAVE IT: "pass1_with_ladder escalates on a CONTEXT-LIMIT signal — it is a SIZE
ladder, not a quality ladder (its own docstring says so). A plan that fits haiku's 200k window stays on
haiku forever."
WHY IT IS SILENT — the loud/quiet asymmetry the ADR should state: "The gates fail CLOSED on errors... That
is the loud path and it is fine. This is the other kind: a haiku Pass-1 that surfaces fewer grounded
findings yields a PASS, which gets signed, and the claim proceeds. The sidecar records only the VERIFIER's
model (data.model), never Pass-1's, so it is invisible in the artifacts too."
NOT TEST-DETECTABLE: "the offline suite substitutes FunctionModel/FakeRunner for exactly the thing that
changes, which is WHICH MODEL a live gate calls." Found by an independent landing-safety assessment.
UNRESOLVED ASYMMETRY WORTH RECORDING: "Code-review's Pass-1 finder declares frontier. Plan-review's Pass-1
declares trivial. Both are finders that generate blocking findings. That asymmetry may be deliberate, but
it has never been effective, so it has never been evaluated."

## 3.7 The bypass census (afeb) — the epic's severity-setting measurement
Config B (classes on Bedrock, cfg.model left bare-Anthropic):
  llm/overlap/judge.py:46            overlap-judge   18 calls  anthropic BYPASS
  llm/enrich.py:81                   ticket-digest    1 call   anthropic BYPASS
  llm/operations.py:177              ticket-quality   1 call   anthropic BYPASS
  llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:571 code-novelty    1 call   anthropic BYPASS
"overlap-judge DOMINATES plan-review traffic — 18 of 23 calls. An operator who cuts over by configuring
the three classes leaves the MAJORITY of plan-review traffic on direct Anthropic."
"ticket-digest IS THE MOST INSIDIOUS... enrich_drain.maybe_drain is called from _store/event_append.py:609
and _store/push.py:295, so it runs on the ticket store WRITE PATH... It therefore sends ticket content to
direct Anthropic during routine store operations, with no gate invocation and nothing in a verdict to
reveal it." Framing: "Bedrock is normally chosen for data-residency, procurement or contractual reasons."
THE TWO-CONFIGURATION METHODOLOGY INVARIANT — MUST NOT BE REDISCOVERED: "Config B — does every call honour
the CLASS configuration? (found 4 that do not). Config A — is any provider HARDCODED past configuration
entirely? (found none). Config A alone is necessary but NOT sufficient: it would have passed even with
every bypass site unfixed... Anyone re-running this later should run BOTH, or the result is a false clean."
Related (b690): "With no model_classes configured, frontier resolves to the built-in claude-opus-4-8 —
which IS cfg.model — so a frontier-declaring step runs on opus whether or not the declaration is honoured."
=> EVERY LIVE PROBE IN THIS EPIC MUST USE A DISCRIMINATING CLASS TABLE.

## 3.8 Observability invariants (for whoever reads a usage log next)
- REBAR_USAGE_LOG is OPT-IN (usage_log.py:29); this cost a criterion on 77ed.
- It is JSONL, not key=value: "usage_log.py:315 writes json.dumps(row) + '\n'. A model= grep matches
  nothing." And a whole-log grep for bedrock:<model> OVER-COUNTS because verdict-JSON fields match too —
  "it told me 4 when the truth was 1."
- step and model_class come from a ContextVar (b690) WHICH RAW THREADS DO NOT INHERIT (8415): "If overlap
  judging is parallelized with a thread pool and the binding is left outside the pool, every judge call
  silently loses its step/model_class attribution. Bind inside the worker, and assert it in a test."
- op for batch steps is the OVERLAY prompt, not the batch.prompt finder — "so the pass a call belongs to is
  recoverable ONLY from step."
- Every row now carries an explicit outcome (8455); pre-8455 rows must be read row.get("outcome","ok").
- AN EMPTY USAGE LOG IS NOT EVIDENCE NO CALL WAS ATTEMPTED (baa8).
- rebar writes ONE usage row per run() aggregating all HTTP calls, with "requests": N (dd27).

## 3.9 Module-size governance (db7f -> ADR 0058), quoted because it IS the ADR rationale
1. "Governance inversion. The 800 cap is deliberately LOCKED. The stricter bounds that actually bind these
   files are bare literals in test files any contributor can edit. The tightest constraint is the least
   governed one."
2. "It breaks the refactors it exists to encourage. A multi-commit decomposition necessarily passes through
   intermediate states where the file has not shrunk yet... This has now happened twice on this epic's
   stack (changes 1121/1122 at runner.py 782, and again after a rebase)."
3. "It has already cost a full investigation once. Bug 3a98 was opened for exactly this."
4. "The duplication is self-locking. test_decide_ops_seam.py:127,130 assert that the literal strings appear
   in another test file's SOURCE TEXT."

## 3.10 Evidence-hygiene rules earned the hard way (a strong ADR appendix)
- ASSERT git status --porcelain IS EMPTY before the suite you intend to cite (48b3): "CI CAUGHT A REAL
  DEFECT THAT EVERY LOCAL RUN MISSED — the test edits were never committed... A suite run against a dirty
  tree is not evidence about the commit."
- Never validate a scoped policy with a wildcard-holding identity — and CHECK THE ACCOUNT (9249).
- A SIMULATOR ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION THAN A REAL CALL (9249, the marquee finding): "the policy
  simulator answers 'what does the policy language permit for the action you NAMED', not 'which action does
  the service actually CHECK'. Only a real call distinguishes those two questions." And: "Evidence is only
  as good as its ability to have come out the other way FOR THE REASON YOU CARE ABOUT."
- VERIFICATION THAT ENCODES ITS OWN BLIND SPOT — a recurring pattern worth naming once: a574's runbook
  passing --region everywhere; dd27's confounded arms reading each other's cache inside the 5-minute TTL;
  7a79's pre-existing test pinned at input_tokens=4029, itself sub-floor; e3cd's test passing the floor as
  a literal rather than reading it from capabilities_for. "In every case the GUARD shared the BUG's
  assumption."
- NEGATIVE-FORM ACs PASS VACUOUSLY. a574: "an AC asserting 'a TYPED error, not a bare NoRegionError' is
  already true today and proves nothing." f81d: "A test that merely asserts 'a cache breakpoint exists'
  passes for the wrong reason."
- SELF-REFERENTIAL ACs DEADLOCK THE CLOSE GATE (f81d): "gate 433c turns any self-referential AC into an
  unbreakable deadlock, and the phrasing that causes it — 'the correct outcome is to close this as X' — is
  natural to write when an author wants to pre-authorise a wont-fix."
- The completion verifier reads REPOSITORY FILES ONLY, never git history (5e75, 0d76) — out-of-repo
  criteria must be tagged [operator-attested] or they burn a close cycle.
- The default test selection EXCLUDES the integration tier where some evidence lives (55bc).
- Do not mutate the working tree while a gating suite runs in it (2932).
- LIVE GATE RUNS EXCEED THE 600s STREAM WATCHDOG on a loaded host (1aa2): "Four consecutive agent attempts
  were killed... the failure was structural rather than bad luck. A background job has no watchdog." And:
  "the previous attempt completed its five calls and then died while writing the record — the calls were
  billed and produced nothing durable."
- A 4-char short id is NOT guaranteed unique (afeb).
- Set file_impact BEFORE a review, never after (3768): "An unscoped attestation dies stale-head on EVERY
  commit, and setting file_impact AFTER a review is a material edit that destroys the PASS."
- deps is NOT the blocker list (3768): "Blocking comes from LINK relations. rebar ready is the
  authoritative claimability check."
- Run the repo checkout's build, not a stale global install (343b).

## 3.11 Cost, latency and volume figures worth preserving
- THE AGENTIC COST FINDING (0d76): plan asserted "at most 360 model calls"; measured "~102k input tokens
  and ~8.6 requests PER case-run." Root cause: "the code-review arm is agentic too... Eight of the fifteen
  sampled specs are code-review specs." FINAL ACTUAL: ~1,400 provider requests / ~15.4M input tokens.
- Full parity corpus: 30 enumerated / 28 scored (later 26 after ed82), N=3 epochs, 360 case-runs,
  corpus_digest 9d707f76..., commit 4214516f95a.
- LATENCY: standard slot Bedrock 9.9% FASTER (2484.6s vs 2756.5s); frontier within 0.1%. RETIRES the N=1
  pilot's "~35% slower" hint, which was self-retracted.
- Validity 1.000 both arms both slots over 360 case-runs; runtime error rate 0.000; v2 arms provably
  provider-clean (ZERO non-Bedrock calls across 84/84 case-runs per slot).
- dd27's O(N^2) PROOF: 9 calls / 8 tool turns, total prompt tokens IDENTICAL at 109,029; cache_read
  11,160 -> 88,244; cache_write 0 -> 20,775; UNCACHED INPUT 97,869 -> 10. Per-call attribution is the
  load-bearing part: "B2 cache_read is FLAT 1,240 on every one of the 9 calls, INDEPENDENT of how much
  history the request carries... Meanwhile uncached input climbs 480 -> 3,093 -> ... -> 21,254. THAT IS THE
  O(N^2) SHAPE, MEASURED." Workload identity: request_bytes differ by "EXACTLY 48 bytes at every step — the
  cache_control directive itself." Fully-warm third run: 99.99% of prompt tokens from cache.
- THE REAL ANTHROPIC CACHE FLOOR IS 1024, NOT 4096 (8415, corroborated c403/e3cd): 622->0/0, 922->0/0,
  1042->write 1035 then read 1035, 1117->cached, 4222->cached. Sharpest consequence (e3cd):
  "claude-opus-4-8 is rebar's DEFAULT_MODEL and its documented floor is 1024, so the 4096 global was 4x too
  high on the model rebar runs most."
- HIDDEN PREFIX COST: "measured per-call input is 1,324 while system + instructions is only 985, so ~339
  tokens of tool/scaffold sit in front."
- CACHE WRITES COST A 1.25x PREMIUM, so parallelizing cold calls that share a prefix is "strictly worse
  than the sequential version it replaced, and worse than no caching at all" (8415). Required shape if ever
  parallelized: one call first to completion, then fan out N-1 readers.
- c403 batching: 12 judge calls -> 2; input 17,558 -> 9,116 (-48.1%); prefix 422 -> 1,337 (clears 1024);
  cache 0/0 -> 1,331/1,331. And which mechanism crossed the floor was NOT the one originally named:
  "Batching by itself adds NOTHING to the cacheable prefix... What lifted it is the BATCH PROTOCOL section
  the prompt now has to carry — count_tokens puts it at +436 tokens."
- 1aa2 local dogfooding on Bedrock: 27 calls, 27/27 provider=bedrock, 0 direct-Anthropic, cache_read
  226,668 / cache_write 33,066. PASS, signable. tier=first_class, native_structured_output=false,
  prompt_cache_style=bedrock, supports_thinking=true. Notable: "Despite native_structured_output=false on
  the Bedrock profile, the run emitted a fully-formed verdict envelope." Revert is one unset.
- THE CANONICAL PER-PASS SPLIT, measured and preserved ACROSS A PROVIDER BOUNDARY (eb58): 41 calls
  anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 (96,055 input) + 1 call bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 (2,857). "THAT
  41/1 SPLIT IS THE DECISIVE RESULT... the per-pass class split survives crossing a provider boundary,
  which is the capability this epic exists to deliver and which no single-scalar REBAR_LLM_MODEL could
  express."
- 1157, verified against the live Models API: haiku-4-5 200,000; sonnet-4-6 1,000,000; opus-4-8 1,000,000.
- 12e4: git low-speed abort at 5.1s / 2.1s vs a 300s ceiling; 3 cold clones of the 80 MB mirror at
  87.8/88.4/101.4s all complete under limit=1000/time=10.
- df2c: "25 consecutive runs of the exact command, 2 hung past 320s (rc=124), the other 23 finished in 1-3s
  ... a connection stall, not a large transfer and not load."

## 4. WHAT docs/llm-framework.md NOW GETS WRONG (file is 661 lines; all line numbers verified)
### 4A FIRST — TWO OF THIS TICKET'S OWN PREMISES ARE FALSE. Fix the ticket before writing the ADR.
1. THE LINE REFERENCES ARE STALE. The provider-support section is 128-166, NOT 121-143. The env table is
   245-258, NOT 224-226 (line 224 is now "## Reviewer registry"). Most importantly, :131-133 is NOT the
   local-server recipe — it is the provider-resolution claim. The recipe is at 150-152.
2. "its :131-133 local-server recipe describes behaviour that only becomes true in S4" is now stale IN THE
   OTHER DIRECTION: S4 HAS LANDED and the recipe WORKS. The refusal is gone. _pai_check_config
   (structured_run.py:576-597) docstring: "VALIDATE base_url/api_key rather than refuse them outright
   (story S4): this used to raise for ANY base_url/api_key, making the OpenAI-compatible local-server
   recipe docs/llm-framework.md documents a false promise."
### 4B Provider resolution — the registry is UNDOCUMENTED (CONTRADICTED)
  :130-133 "The pydantic-ai runner is provider-agnostic: pydantic-ai resolves the provider from the model
    string" — contradicted by providers.py:106-109/:132-176 (rebar builders FIRST at :160-166, pydantic-ai
    only as step 2 at :168-172, typed LLMConfigError at :176) and config.py:214-241/:244-261. Should say:
    rebar OWNS a provider registry that intercepts infer_model; pydantic-ai's resolution is the FALLBACK;
    an unrecognized qualifier is a typed LLMConfigError.
  :120 runner table — same, plus config.py:450-453 (no Bedrock credential field). Credentials are
    per-provider; Bedrock holds NO rebar key.
  :88 and :105 (ASCII diagram) — should name ProviderSession.
### 4C AWS BEDROCK IS ABSENT ENTIRELY (MISSING). grep -in bedrock docs/llm-framework.md => ZERO HITS.
  Meanwhile: registry slot providers.py:108; builder bedrock_model.py:41; KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES members

## 5. THE TIER MODEL
### 5.1 There is NO enum and NO Literal type. The tier is two bare string literals from ONE expression:
    capabilities.py:439  "tier": "best_effort" if (base_url or via_gateway) else "first_class",
  Spellings first_class / best_effort. grep across src/ returns only capabilities.py:403,415,416,439.
### 5.2 What DETERMINES it — two independent triggers, and NOT registry membership
  (1) base_url truthy -> best_effort. (2) via_gateway = provider in _GATEWAY_PROVIDER_NAMES
  (capabilities.py:434) -> best_effort. That frozenset is five exact ids (:384-392).
  IMPORTANT NUANCE: the tier is NOT a per-registry-entry field and NOT ProviderSession._builders
  membership. It is membership in a SEPARATE frozenset plus the base_url predicate. Everything else
  defaults to first_class — INCLUDING AN UNREGISTERED PROVIDER NAME.
### 5.3 What "first class" MEANS as a policy commitment
  Epic: "First-class = Anthropic + Bedrock: native builders, full fidelity, covered by tests and the parity
  bar. Best-effort = everything else through one OpenAI-compatible builder."
  "FULL FIDELITY" WAS EXPLICITLY REDEFINED BY THE EPIC: "Retry and timeout on Bedrock are botocore's, not
  httpx's... 'Full fidelity' for the first-class tier therefore means EQUIVALENT retry and timeout
  guarantees achieved PER TRANSPORT, not the same transport object on both providers."
  *** CRITICAL HONESTY FINDING — THAT CLAIM IS CURRENTLY UNBACKED BY CODE. *** The epic says the Bedrock
  builder constructs its client with botocore.config.Config(retries={"max_attempts":
  cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts, "mode": "adaptive"}) and gets its read bound from
  BedrockProvider(aws_read_timeout=cfg.timeout_s, aws_connect_timeout=10.0), concluding "The retry-attempt
  count and the read timeout are thus driven by the SAME LLMConfig fields on both first-class providers."
  NONE OF THAT SHIPPED. Verified: grep -rn "botocore.config|BotoConfig|aws_read_timeout|retry_mode|
  max_attempts" src/rebar/llm/ returns ONLY config.py and anthropic_model.py hits — no botocore Config, no
  "adaptive" mode, no aws_read_timeout anywhere in src/ or tests/. The whole construction is
  bedrock_model.py:88 -> return BedrockProvider(region_name=region). Bedrock inherits botocore's STOCK
  defaults while the Anthropic path owns an explicit tenacity envelope.
  => THE RETRY/TIMEOUT HALF OF "first_class = full fidelity" IS AN UNMET INTENTION, NOT A LANDED PROPERTY.
     Either say so in the ADR, or file it. It also means S6's "same LLMConfig fields drive both" parity
     claim was never measurable as written — separately moot, since S6 was rescoped away by OD4.
  AND THE PARITY HALF WAS RESCOPED. Under OD4, "covered by the parity bar" now means payload/tool/routing
  parity, not verdict parity. 0d76: "BEDROCK CLEARS THE BAR AS THE EPIC DEFINES IT: same payloads reach the
  LLM, same tools are available, routing is provider-clean, and both inference profiles invoke."
  WITH A NUANCE THAT WILL CONFUSE A READER OF THE ARTIFACT: "the residual gating_failures (standard 1 flip;
  frontier agreement 0.929 + 2 flips) are cross-model verdict comparisons and are INFORMATIONAL, not gates.
  Both slots therefore carry passed=False while no acceptance criterion is unmet."
### 5.4 What "best effort" MEANS: an intermediary may have rewritten the request and rebar cannot vouch for
  what reached the model. capabilities.py:409-418. Reached through ONE OpenAI-compatible builder
  (providers.py:235-290) with supports_json_schema_output deliberately WITHDRAWN (:256-272) — a deliberate
  capability DOWNGRADE as part of what best-effort means.
### 5.5 What a consumer can infer — AND FOUR LOAD-BEARING CAVEATS
  Stated in-tree (test_verdict_provenance.py:217-218): "The two-tier field exists so an attestation
  consumer can reject an off-tier verdict; a wrong tier makes it worthless."
  A consumer reads (capabilities.py:435-446): provider, model (provider-qualified), endpoint_host (HOST
  ONLY — .hostname never .netloc, so user:secret@ cannot enter a signed record), tier, and capabilities
  (exactly four: native_structured_output, prompt_cache_style, supports_thinking, supports_temperature).
  cache_min_prefix_tokens deliberately NOT carried (D28). On a fallback chain, plus candidates and
  ran_model.
  CAVEAT 1 — THE TIER IS DERIVED PURELY FROM CONFIGURATION-TIME FACTS, NEVER FROM AN OBSERVED ENDPOINT. A
    first_class stamp does NOT prove where traffic went. Two concrete holes: an ambient ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
    loopback proxy is BYPASSED rather than recorded (providers.py:190-197), and an unregistered/nonsense
    provider name stamps first_class by default.
  CAVEAT 2 — THE TIER IS NOT IN THE SIGNED BYTES. It is in the adjacent, UNSIGNED sidecar payload. 343b
    verbatim: "The sidecar payload is NOT what gets signed. Signing binds (ticket_id, manifest), where the
    manifest is a list of 'key: value' strings, and model enters via a separate channel... So 'the
    signature still verifies' is about the MANIFEST, not the payload — and if provenance is also meant to
    enter the signed bytes, THAT IS A SECOND, DELIBERATE DECISION." NOWHERE IS THAT DECISION MADE.
    Corroborated at test_verdict_provenance.py:186-191. Precedent for how it COULD be done without
    invalidating prior signatures: test_attestation_signing.py:285,311 (the rebar-version stamp).
    => TREAT 343b's TITLE ("verdicts stamp provider/endpoint/tier") AND ITS CLOSING PHRASE "stamped it into
       the signed payload" AS LOOSE. Whether a consumer can CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY trust the tier was never
       established.
  CAVEAT 3 — ABSENCE IS OVERLOADED and the two meanings are INDISTINGUISHABLE. By D22 absence means
    "unknown, legacy"; by D24/D8 it ALSO means "no model ran / no provider resolved." 343b accepts this:
    "Always-present-but-None reads as 'no provider record for this call', which downstream carries as an
    ABSENT verdict key — identical to a runner that stamped nothing."
  CAVEAT 4 — NO CONSUMER EXISTS. 343b's claim that "a consumer now has the lever" is an ASSERTION: no
    consumer was built, none is named, and no test asserts a consumer can act on tier.
  BEWARE A NAME COLLISION: plan_review/sidecar.py:557 "tier": f.get("tier") is a FINDING tier inside
  _slim(), entirely unrelated to the provider tier. Flagged at design time: "The 'tier' token elsewhere
  (review_kernel/decide.py, pass1.py) is impact-scoring / DET-vs-LLM and is unrelated — do not overload it."
### 5.6 The tier's own biggest near-miss, which is good ADR material
  343b GAP 5: "THE WIRING IS INCOMPLETE IN PRODUCTION. Found by the [operator-attested] criterion, which is
  exactly what that criterion exists for." A real rebar review-plan wrote a sidecar with model:
  claude-sonnet-4-6 and provider_provenance: ABSENT — "So the field never reaches a production payload,
  even though all 10 unit tests pass." Why the tests missed it: "every test hands build_payload a verdict
  dict that ALREADY contains provider_provenance... This is a textbook constructed-input pass: the oracle
  proved the persist step, not the path." The guard that now protects it:
  test_a_real_coach_verdict_survives_into_the_sidecar_payload — "No hand-built verdict anywhere in the
  file." NOTE: at 343b's close the CODE-REVIEW gate's provenance was known-broken and deferred to e951.
